scope: One shared Embassy SHA-256/HMAC-SHA-256 registration uses existing erasing Charlotte hash owners for connector TLS as well as management certificate fingerprints. Stock registrations are removed from normal and management-test dependency graphs. No cryptographic algorithm, wire format, entropy authority, deadline or capability policy change.

ownership_contract.selection: ZeroizeOnDrop bounds qualify actual driver associated context types; duplicate exported symbols reject stock registration.
ownership_contract.forwarding: Pinned unitrait bb96601b3d293fa27d1ca2891f6ea148e534e433 generates Drop forwarding through drop_in_place of the concrete Context, consuming argument moves through ManuallyDrop, and concrete Clone forwarding. Its macro checks opaque storage size/alignment.
ownership_contract.outputs: Driver-local digest/tag temporaries retain zeroizing owners; the plain ABI output belongs to its TLS caller.
ownership_contract.baseline_limit: The previous stock contexts lacked the selected erasure policy. No new retained-memory measurement of those old opaque contexts was performed.

host_validation.selected_suite: Actual embedded-tls associated hash/HMAC types match independent SHA-256/HMAC vectors through incremental update, clones and tamper rejection; the same control runs in the signed native probe.
host_validation.interop: OpenSSL and Rustls/ring host controls cover connector/server authentication, mTLS, wire tamper and interruption.

limits: No new opaque-context padding, target-memory, register/spill or allocator-history erasure measurement. Concrete Drop/Clone forwarding is a pinned source/type contract backed by shared-owner field tests.

Embedded-tls PRK/traffic-key/IV fields, Rustls outputs, signature-library intermediates and other hash families retain their separate lifetime gaps. Ordinary Drop cannot promise erasure after forced termination or physical teardown.
Finite S3/TLS and management/security cases do not establish sustained pressure fairness, throughput, physical-platform qualification or custody.
SEC-15 remains partial; finding counts and historical unresolved incident attributions are unchanged.
